prize_parts.citation: For experimental and theoretical-pathway analysis of long-range electron transfer through proteins, establishing the physical principles of biological redox chains

statement.case_for: Gray and Winkler's tunnelling work with azurin, cytochrome c and Ru-labelled proteins turned Marcus theory into a quantitative, distance-dependent description of how electrons move through protein media. This is the physical mechanism behind respiratory and photosynthetic energy conversion, and the principles (tunnelling timetables, reorganization energy, hopping through redox-active residues) are used well beyond the original proteins. The attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist: two names, one programme, four decades of reproduced results, and no competition for a third seat. Several higher-ranked candidacies spread credit over five to eight people, whereas this is a named, attributable body of experiments.
statement.case_against: The 1992 Marcus prize may be judged to have already recognised the conceptual core, so this could be read as the experimental half of an existing prize. Dutton, Moser, Beratan, Onuchic and Hopfield have priority claims on tunnelling-pathway ideas that I have not verified, and nobody else on the committee ranked B055 in their top eight. Its opening support is the thinnest on the shortlist, and I must acknowledge that the field's biophysical emphasis matches my own bias.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B019 fourth, asks what is chemically new, and notes the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands are separate with no approved PROTAC drug yet, so recognition may be early.
responses.response: I agree with the maturity and attribution concerns and they are why I ranked B019 seventh. Eight credited names across two discoveries (heterobifunctional design versus cereblon as the thalidomide target) cannot be honestly compressed into three without ignoring one strand. I disagree only mildly on chemical novelty: the induced-ternary-complex principle is real and mechanistically well defined. B019 is a strong field, but I would want the expert reports to show whether PROTAC and glue contributions can be separated, since a two-part prize is blocked by the three-person limit.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B019 first as a general, mechanistically defined design principle, and ranks B046 fourth, noting that nitrogenase structures are confirmed but the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding states remain debated.
responses.response: On B046 I fully agree: the carbide and cofactor structures are secure, but the N2-reduction mechanism is not, so a prize would honour structure rather than mechanism. That keeps it behind B055 for me, even though the attribution among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe is also unsettled. On B019 I accept that confirmation across labs is extensive, but I do not think breadth of impact alone settles a credit that the committee cannot split cleanly. I would ask what the field reports say about Handa versus Ciulli before I move.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranks nanopore sequencing B002 first as a clear physical principle turned into a practical capability, while conceding the credit is spread across more than three people.
responses.response: I recognise the strength of the physical principle and the maturity, but I think the attribution problem is serious, not a footnote: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer (1996 translocation), Bayley (engineered pores), and Akeson (enzymatic ratcheting) each have a distinct decisive step, and any trio omits one of them. I would want the expert report to settle whether the central discovery is the principle or the enzyme-controlled reading before supporting B002 over a compact attribution such as B055. I did not rank it in my top eight for that reason and would not call it an overdue sure thing.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B019 first as a new drug modality and B043 second, and treats Ciulli as essential to the PROTAC credit alongside Crews and Deshaies.
responses.response: Johan and I joined the committee together and I respect his emphasis on chemical mechanism, but I would qualify the Ciulli choice: VHL ligand design and structural rigour were important, yet Handa's identification of cereblon is a distinct discovery explaining the clinical glue drugs. Choosing Ciulli over Handa implicitly chooses the PROTAC strand and demotes a mechanism that underlies a marketed drug class. This should be debated explicitly, not decided by default.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the 1992 Marcus prize to have already covered the conceptual core of protein electron transfer.
Priority of Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic on tunnelling pathways, which I have not verified from the expert reports.
Whether B019 can be split into PROTAC and molecular-glue strands within the three-person cap, and whether the lack of an approved PROTAC makes it premature.
Whether the nitrogenase (B046) mechanism is resolved enough to prefer it over a structure-only award.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional conflict with the B055 candidates is apparent from my profile. My research on proton and electron transfer in cytochrome c oxidase is scientifically close to B055, so my bias toward this field should be weighed. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, but that has no bearing on any shortlisted candidate beyond collegiality.
